import.title: Import a pipeline

settings.title: Pipeline settings
registry.title: Stage registry
registry.note: The registry comes from the backend at {url}. Reload it after the backend has registered new stages; a file is for working on a graph while that backend is down.
secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.lead: Keys are kept apart from the pipeline: only the NAME stays in the JSON, in an export and on the cards, and the value is substituted at start. A node reads it like an ordinary variable — put the name into the "vars" bucket of a stage argument.
secrets.from.env.hint: the value lives in the server environment and never reaches the browser
secrets.from.browser.hint: the value lies in the localStorage of this browser
secrets.drop.env: set by an environment variable of the server
secrets.badName: A secret name is like a variable name: letters, digits, underscore.
secrets.emptyValue: An empty value is not saved: to remove a key, delete it from the list.
secrets.note: This is not encryption: the browser store is readable by extensions and devtools. It protects against the key spreading through exports, screenshots and the debug log. For a real secret use the environment variables of the server (SF_SECRETS=NAME or SF_SECRET_NAME=value): the browser receives the name only.
conn.title: Connection
conn.backend.note: Changing the address reloads the page: it is the ground everything stands on — the stage registry, a running session, the names of the environment secrets.
conn.backend.https: This page is served over https, so it can only reach an https backend — or one on localhost, which browsers allow. A plain http address elsewhere is blocked before the request is made, and looks from here exactly like a backend that is switched off.
conn.auth.rejected: {reason} — the previous credential is still in use.
conn.auth.note: Sent with every request the editor makes. The name is a field because backends disagree — Authorization, X-Api-Key, whatever a gateway reads — and the editor authenticates nothing itself: it carries what it is given. Empty means it sends none. Kept in this browser's localStorage; treat it like the secret store, not like encryption.
conn.plan.note: What the editor draws and validates against: the palette, the limits in the debug panel and the warnings in the status bar. A view, not an entitlement — what a run may do the backend decides from your credentials, and a graph prepared for a plan you are not on is refused when it starts, by name.
conn.plan.same: the same, asked for by name
conn.answer.none: This backend serves no /api/meta, so the editor cannot tell what it runs — and does not guess: nothing is marked unsupported.
connect.lead: The editor draws and debugs pipelines, but the stages and the execution live on a StageFlow backend. Give it the address of one.
connect.auth.note: Sent with every request, this one included. The name is a field because backends disagree: Authorization, X-Api-Key, whatever a gateway reads. Kept in this browser's localStorage — treat it like the secret store, not like encryption.
connect.none: No backend at hand? {command} from {repo} serves one at {url}.
connect.badAddress: That does not look like an address. Try http://host:port.
connect.silentFail: {address} — {reason}. Check the address or start the backend.
palette.noStages: No stages loaded. Menu File → Stage registry…
kind.entry.about: The start of the pipeline: the variables it starts with
kind.condition.about: Branching on a CEL condition: then / else
kind.switch.about: N-way branching: the first true case wins
kind.parallel.about.cancel: The branches run in parallel; one failing cancels the rest
kind.parallel.about.keep: The branches run in parallel; one failing does not cancel the rest
kind.subpipeline.about: A nested pipeline: its own context, exchange through inputs/artifacts
kind.terminal.about: The end of execution: returns result and artifacts
kind.try.about: An error in any node of the body goes to a matching except
kind.map.about.serial: The body runs once per element of the list, one after another
kind.map.about.parallel: The body runs once per element of the list, all elements at once
badge.expose: expose: a copy of a variable under another name
field.expose: copy a variable under another name (expose)
field.consume: drop from the frame after the step (consume)
field.cases: branches: the first true one wins (cases)
field.cancelBranches: cancel sibling branches on a failure (cancel_on_error)
field.collect: what to take out of an iteration (collect)
field.cancelItems: stop the remaining elements on a failure (cancel_on_error)
field.secretHint: a secret from the store: the value is substituted at start
issue.selfLoop: the '{port}' link points at this very node: a loop with no way out
issue.noWayOut: from here a run can no longer end: no path leads to a finish — {nodes}
issue.exposeName: expose '{name}' must be a variable name
issue.manyEntries: more than one entry node: also {nodes}
issue.intoEntry: a transition into the entry point is not allowed: '{node}' refers to it
issue.unknownStage: stage '{stage}' is not in the registry
issue.noSuchOutput: the stage does not return the field '{name}' (it has: {available})
issue.noCase: at least one case is needed
issue.noBranch: at least one branch is needed
issue.noTryBody: no entry into the block body (body) is set
issue.noHandler: at least one except handler is needed
issue.handlerNoNext: an except handler has no transition
issue.noMapBody: no entry into the loop body (body) is set
issue.sameVarNames: item_var and index_var are the same name
issue.collectName: collect '{name}' must be a variable name
issue.escapesLoop: '{node}' leads to '{target}', outside the loop body
issue.entryMissing: entry '{entry}' is not in the graph
issue.entryMismatch: entry '{entry}' does not match the entry node '{node}'
group.more: More: node name, entry, retries, copies
panel.varsNone: — none: the nodes pass nothing to each other yet —
panel.varHover: hover a line — the path of that variable lights up on the canvas
panel.varNoWriter: nobody writes this variable — the reader will get nothing
panel.varNoReader: nobody reads this variable — the write goes nowhere
panel.legend: Arrows are the execution order, colored dots are the variable flows.
panel.tip.1: Pull a wire from the bottom port of a card: onto a node it links them, into empty space it offers to create a node there.
panel.tip.2: A click on a port takes the wire until the next click — Esc lets it go.
panel.tip.3: Hover a link: ⊕ inserts a node into it, × cuts it.
panel.tip.4: A node from the palette can be dragged: onto a link it is inserted into it, onto a card it is attached after it.
panel.tip.5: A double click on empty space creates a node right there.
panel.tip.6: The middle button pans, the right one draws a selection marquee; Shift-click adds a node to the selection.
panel.tip.7: Delete removes what is selected: a single node as well as a whole group.
panel.tip.8: Ctrl+Z undoes an edit, Ctrl+Shift+Z brings it back; the same is in the Edit menu.
panel.tip.9: Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V copy, cut and paste nodes under the cursor.
panel.tip.10: The handle on the panel edge folds it away; the same handle at the edge of the canvas brings it back (or just click a node — its panel unfolds by itself).
panel.tip.11: Shift+F fits the graph into the screen, Shift+L lays it out again; the rest is in the menu bar.
panel.selected.about: Drag any of them and all of them move. Delete removes the selected ones.
panel.entryOwned: the entry point is set by the entry node '{node}'
args.extra.ok: additional arguments: the stage accepts any
args.extra.ok.hint: the stage accepts any additional arguments
args.extra.unknown: the stage did not declare such arguments
args.extra.unknown.hint: the stage did not declare such an argument — it will receive it, but if it does not read it, the value simply goes unused
args.noSpec: no stage selected, or its spec is not loaded
outs.unknownField: the stage does not return such a field — it gives: {available}
outs.exprHint: a pipeline variable: the value is computed by the expression, the stage has nothing to do with it
outs.exprEmpty: set an expression — for example `5`, `vars.n + 1` or `output.value`
spec.title: stage spec
spec.unknownStage: the stage is not in the registry
canvas.insertNode: insert a node into this edge
canvas.empty.1: Double-click the background to create a node.
canvas.empty.2: Then pull a wire from the bottom port of a card: dropping it into empty space asks what to create there.
canvas.region: the area of node {node} — drag to move it
canvas.noSelfLink: a node cannot lead into itself — a loop with no way out
canvas.createConnected.hint: the new node appears here and becomes the target of the port
canvas.insertOnEdge.hint: the node will stand between them, the link is kept
canvas.varToNode.hint: the node will receive this variable
canvas.dragging: {port}: drop it on a node or into empty space
canvas.armed: {port}: click a node or empty space · Esc — cancel
debug.delayHint: the pause between nodes; applied at once, without a restart
debug.varSecret: a secret from the store: the value is hidden and cannot be edited
debug.varEditable: the value is applied before the next node
debug.dropVar: drop the variable from the frame
debug.addVar: add a variable to the frame
rundlg.lead: The starting variables are declared by the node "{node}". An empty field means the value from the pipeline; a filled one overrides it for this run.
rundlg.leadNoEntry: There is no entry node in the graph: the starting variables can be set here.
rundlg.secrets: The store will substitute: {names} — values are not shown.

rundlg.secretsUnused.one: The store holds {n} key, but the graph refers to it nowhere. A node reads a key like a variable: the name in the "vars" argument of a stage must match the name in File → Secrets…
rundlg.secretsUnused.other: The store holds {n} keys, but the graph refers to none of them. A node reads a key like a variable: the name in the "vars" argument of a stage must match the name in File → Secrets…

rundlg.celHint: computed by an expression; fill it in to substitute a ready value
rundlg.constHint: the default value from the entry node
rundlg.paceHint: the pause between nodes in seconds: with it you can see execution walk through the graph. A fraction can be typed with a dot or a comma.
editor.name: editor {version}
editor.previewing: showing plan '{plan}' — a preview; a run goes on whatever your credentials allow
editor.clickToChange: click to change the backend, the credential or the plan
editor.pasteEntry: nothing to paste: the graph already has an entry point
caps.planRefuses: plan '{plan}'{shown} does not include a '{type}' node
caps.coreLacks: the backend (core {version}) does not offer a '{type}' node
caps.backendLacks: the backend does not offer a '{type}' node
caps.tooManySteps: the shortest way through this graph is {nodes} nodes, and the backend allows {steps} steps
caps.tooManyRetries: retry asks for {asked} attempts, and the backend allows {allowed}
caps.retryTooSlow: retry waits {asked}s between attempts, and the backend allows {allowed}s
backend.timeout: the backend did not answer in time
backend.unreachable: the backend is not reachable (is it running, and does it allow CORS?)
backend.notJson: the answer is not JSON — is this a StageFlow backend?
backend.noStages: the answer has no stages — is this a StageFlow backend?
bridge.localNetwork: the browser did not let this page reach an address on your machine. Allow it when asked, or open the editor from that machine instead (it is served at 127.0.0.1 when you run it yourself)
bridge.about: an agent outside the browser is working on this graph: what it draws lands here, what you draw is sent back, and undo takes back anything it did
